 Print Sixers vs. Bulls preview. Image via: NBA The 6-1 Philadelphia 76ers host the Chicago Bulls on Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, with tip-off set for 7:30 p.m. EST. It is a short stay at home. The Sixers fly to Detroit on Wednesday to open a three-game road trip that also stops in Cleveland and Chicago. Jaylen Brown, the veteran forward who missed Friday’s win over the New York Knicks, was left off the weekend injury report and looks set to start. Joel Embiid is listed as questionable with right foot plantar fascia injury management. Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukporti are out. Chicago may be without Nic Claxton, who is doubtful. Here is where to watch, who is hurt and who is expected to start. Sixers vs. Bulls: Game preview
 Philadelphia’s 6-1 start has included some rallies. The Sixers have won games from behind, and they would rather stop needing to. The aim against Chicago is one clean game over all 48 minutes. The schedule adds some push, since three straight road games follow, at Detroit, Cleveland and Chicago, before the team gets back to Philadelphia. Jaylen Brown’s knee is the main thing to watch. A left patellar tendinopathy sidelined the veteran forward for Friday’s win over the Knicks, his first missed game of the season. Brown returned on Halloween and played 38 minutes in a 109-104 win over Charlotte. The numbers were modest: 16 points, four assists and four rebounds on 40.0% shooting. All four sat below the averages from the first five games, when the forward put up 20.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 4.2 assists in 36.4 minutes a night, shooting 44.2% overall and 40.9% from three. The same knee trouble showed up earlier in Brown’s career with the Celtics. Coach Nick Nurse suggested the latest setback is not a long-term concern, and Philadelphia left Brown off its first injury report for this game. Barring a change, he starts. Chicago’s projected group has Josh Giddey and Norman Powell in the backcourt, Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis up front, and Jalen Smith at center. How to watch Sixers vs. Bulls game on Monday?
 The game is on NBC Sports Philadelphia, with tip-off at 7:30 p.m. EST. Philadelphia wears its blue Icon Edition uniforms. Chicago is in the red Icon Edition set. Join conversation

 Two things are worth watching early. Embiid’s status is the first, and it is the one to check closest to tip-off. The second is how the Sixers start. A fast first quarter would be a change from the games they have had to rescue. Sixers vs. Bulls: date, time, and venue
 Date: Monday, Nov. 2
 Time: 7:30 p.m. EST
 Venue: Xfinity Mobile Arena, Philadelphia, PA
 TV channel: NBC Sports Philadelphia
 Sixers vs. Bulls: Injury Report
 Philadelphia 76ers Out: Dominick Barlow (low back stress reaction)
 Out: Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tear)
 Questionable: Joel Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management)
 Brown is not listed after coming back against the Hornets. Chicago Bulls Doubtful: Nic Claxton (left hamstring strain)
 Probable: Jalen Smith (left finger sprain)
 Probable: Tobe Awaka (left ankle sprain)
 Claxton’s doubtful tag makes Smith’s availability matter more. Smith is the projected starting center, finger sprain and all. Sixers vs. Bulls: Probable starting lineups
 Philadelphia 76ers Guard: Tyrese Maxey
 Guard: VJ Edgecombe
 Forward: Jaylen Brown
 Forward: LeBron James
 Center: Joel Embiid
 Chicago Bulls Guard: Josh Giddey
 Guard: Norman Powell
 Forward: Caleb Wilson
 Forward: Matas Buzelis
 Center: Jalen Smith
 These lineups are probable and may change before tip-off, especially with Embiid questionable.
